steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement that imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package in a single import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using an import statement.

steps.title: Create the main Tabs component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named 'Tabs' that accepts children as props. Define a TypeScript interface for its props and use it to type the component parameter.
steps.hint: Start by defining an interface for the props, then create either a function or arrow function component that uses that interface.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Tabs component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Tabs component is defined with typed props, ready to be used as a container.
successCriteria: Uses a TypeScript interface for props
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Tabs component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure to define an interface for the props and use it to type the component parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs component is missing or incomplete. Remember to define an interface for props and create a component that accepts children.

steps.title: Create the TabList component
steps.instruction: Create a TabList functional component that accepts children as props. Define a TypeScript interface for its props and return the children wrapped in a <div> element.
steps.hint: Define an interface for props with a children property of type React.ReactNode, then create either a function or arrow function component named TabList that uses this interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TabList component is created with proper TypeScript typing that can accept and render children.
successCriteria: Props include children of type React.ReactNode
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TabList component with proper TypeScript typing. This component will serve as the container for your tab buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've: 1) Defined a TabList component, 2) Created an interface for props with children, 3) Properly typed the children as React.ReactNode, and 4) Returned the children wrapped in JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabList component isn't properly defined. Remember to create a functional component named TabList that accepts children as props with TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Create the Tab component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Tab that accepts children as props. Define a TypeScript interface for its props.
steps.hint: Define an interface for the props, then create a component that returns its children.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Tab component is created with typed props interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Tab component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined both the interface and the component that accepts children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tab component isn't properly defined. Check that you've created both the interface and the component.

steps.title: Create the TabPanels component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TabPanels that accepts children as props. Define a TypeScript interface for the props and return the children wrapped in a div.
steps.hint: Define an interface for the component props, then create a component that receives children and renders them inside a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TabPanels component is created with proper TypeScript typing that can accept and render children content.
successCriteria: Returns JSX with children wrapped in div
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TabPanels component with proper TypeScript typing. This component will serve as the container for your tab content panels.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you define a TypeScript interface for the props? Does your component accept children and return them wrapped in a div?
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanels component isn't quite right. Remember to create a functional component named TabPanels that accepts children as props with a TypeScript interface and returns the children inside a div element.

steps.title: Create the TabPanel component
steps.instruction: Create a TabPanel component as a functional component that accepts children as props. Define a TypeScript interface for its props.
steps.hint: Define an interface for the props (e.g., TabPanelProps) with a children property, then create a component that returns its children wrapped in a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TabPanel component is defined with typed props and returns its children inside a div.
successCriteria: The code includes a TabPanel component with a TypeScript interface for props and returns children in JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TabPanel component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined both the interface and the component that returns its children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanel component is missing or incomplete. Check that you've defined an interface and a component that returns children.

steps.title: Add active tab state to Tabs component
steps.instruction: Initialize an activeTab state variable in your Tabs component using useState, defaulting to 0.
steps.hint: Use useState<number>(0) to create a state variable that tracks which tab is currently active.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component will have an activeTab state variable initialized to 0.
successCriteria: The Tabs component should include a useState call that creates an activeTab state variable with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the activeTab state to track which tab is currently selected.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've properly initialized the activeTab state with useState<number>(0).
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs component doesn't have the activeTab state yet. Add useState<number>(0) inside the Tabs component.

steps.title: Create context for sharing active tab state
steps.instruction: Create a React context named TabsContext using React.createContext. Export it and provide proper TypeScript typing for the context value.
steps.hint: Use React.createContext to create a context. Define the type for the context value (an object with activeTab and setActiveTab properties). Export the context so it can be used in other components.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a properly typed TabsContext created and exported, ready to share the active tab state between components.
successCriteria: Define TypeScript interface/type for context value
Include activeTab and setActiveTab in context type
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed React context. This will allow the Tabs, Tab, and TabPanel components to share the active tab state without prop drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are a few things missing. Make sure you've: 1) Used React.createContext, 2) Defined a TypeScript type for the context value that includes both activeTab and setActiveTab, and 3) Exported the context so other components can use it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a React context using React.createContext. The context should have a TypeScript type that includes both the activeTab value and the setActiveTab function. Don't forget to export it.

steps.title: Wrap Tabs children with context provider
steps.instruction: Inside the Tabs component, wrap the children prop with the TabsContext.Provider component. Pass an object with 'activeTab' and 'setActiveTab' as the value prop.
steps.hint: Return <TabsContext.Provider value={{ activeTab, setActiveTab }}>{children}</TabsContext.Provider> from the Tabs component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component now provides the activeTab state and setter to all child components via context.
successCriteria: value prop includes activeTab and setActiveTab
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the Tabs children with the context provider, making the active tab state available to all child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're wrapping the children prop with TabsContext.Provider and passing both activeTab and setActiveTab in the value object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs component should return a TabsContext.Provider that wraps the children prop, with value={{ activeTab, setActiveTab }}.

steps.title: Make Tab component interactive with click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the Tab component, add an onClick handler to the button that uses the context to set the active tab when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the context value's setActiveTab function in the onClick handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tab component's button will have an onClick handler that updates the active tab when clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an onClick handler to the Tab component that uses the context to update the active tab.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the context's setActiveTab function in the onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tab component needs an onClick handler that calls the context's setActiveTab function when clicked.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering to TabPanel component
steps.instruction: In the TabPanel component, add conditional rendering so it only renders its children when its index matches the active tab value from context.
steps.hint: Use the useContext hook to access the activeTab value from TabsContext, then compare it with the TabPanel's index prop. Return the children only if they match, otherwise return null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TabPanel component will now only display its content when its index matches the active tab, hiding all other panels.
successCriteria: TabPanel component uses useContext to access TabsContext
Returns children only when activeTab === index
Returns null when they don't match
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to the TabPanel component. Now each panel will only show when its index matches the active tab.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're: 1) using useContext to get activeTab from TabsContext, 2) comparing it with the index prop, and 3) returning null when they don't match.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanel component needs to conditionally render based on the active tab. Use useContext to access TabsContext, compare activeTab with the index prop, and return children only when they match.

steps.title: Export all compound components
steps.instruction: Export the Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanels, and TabPanel components so they can be imported and used together.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before each component declaration or add export statements at the end of the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: All five components are exported, making the compound component pattern usable.
successCriteria: The Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanels, and TabPanel components must be exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported all compound components. Now they can be imported and used together as a cohesive tabs component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You exported some components, but not all five. Make sure to export Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanels, and TabPanel.
steps.feedbackWrong: The components are not exported correctly. Use export statements to make Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanels, and TabPanel available for import.
